sections.heading: Upheal vs AutoNotes: Overview
sections.content: Upheal and AutoNotes are both AI documentation tools for therapists, but they work very differently. Upheal uses ambient AI to record sessions in real-time and provides unique session analytics (talking ratios, sentiment trends, silence detection) that no other scribe offers. AutoNotes uses typed prompts and checkbox-based input for post-session documentation, making it the cheapest option at $24/month but requiring more manual work. Both are mental health specific and HIPAA compliant.

sections.heading: Pricing Comparison
sections.content: AutoNotes is the cheapest AI therapy scribe at $24/month (annual) for 30 notes, or $49/month for unlimited notes on the Pro plan. Upheal offers a free tier (typed notes only), a Starter plan at $19/month for 50 notes, and Premium at $69/month for 100 notes with full analytics. Upheal's unique pay-per-session model ($1/session capped at $69) works well for low-volume practitioners. AutoNotes wins on pure price; Upheal wins on flexibility.

sections.heading: Feature Differences
sections.content: The key differentiator is session analytics. Upheal provides real-time analysis of talking ratios, sentiment trends, speech patterns, and silence detection-insights no other scribe offers. Upheal's Golden Thread feature tracks client progress session-to-session. AutoNotes has no session analytics-it's purely a documentation tool. Upheal also includes built-in HIPAA-compliant telehealth video; AutoNotes does not. However, AutoNotes supports more note format types (12+) and has a larger user base (80,000+ vs 36,000+).

sections.heading: Workflow Comparison
sections.content: Upheal records sessions live and generates notes in under 60 seconds. You can use Upheal's built-in telehealth or integrate with Zoom, Google Meet, or Doxy.me. AutoNotes requires you to type session recaps, use checkbox templates, or upload audio after sessions-it's post-session documentation, not real-time. For high-volume practitioners, Upheal's ambient approach saves time. For those who prefer manual control over documentation input, AutoNotes' typed approach gives you that control.

sections.heading: EHR Integration
sections.content: Upheal has native integrations with SimplePractice, TherapyNotes, and Jane App that auto-populate notes directly into your EHR. AutoNotes uses copy-paste or a Chrome extension-there's no native API integration. This means AutoNotes adds manual overhead as your caseload grows, while Upheal's workflow scales better.

faqs.q: Does AutoNotes record therapy sessions like Upheal?
faqs.a: No. AutoNotes uses typed prompts and checkbox templates-you document after sessions by typing recaps or uploading audio. Upheal uses real-time ambient AI that records sessions live. If you want live session recording, use Upheal or Mentalyc, not AutoNotes.

faqs.q: What session analytics does Upheal provide that AutoNotes doesn't?
faqs.a: Upheal provides unique real-time analytics including talking ratio, sentiment trends, speech patterns, silence detection, and topic frequency. These help you understand therapeutic dynamics objectively. AutoNotes has no session analytics-it only generates notes from your input.

faqs.q: Which has better EHR integration: Upheal or AutoNotes?
faqs.a: Upheal has native integrations with SimplePractice, TherapyNotes, and Jane App that auto-populate notes. AutoNotes only offers copy-paste or Chrome extension insertion-no native API integration. Upheal's integrations scale better as caseloads grow.

faqs.q: Can I use Upheal or AutoNotes for telehealth sessions?
faqs.a: Upheal has built-in HIPAA-compliant telehealth video with integrated AI recording. AutoNotes does not include telehealth-you would use a separate platform (Zoom, Doxy.me) and then manually document afterward.
